description:
Advances: ancora.review
Ready-for: implement

Problem: on PRs the shared Elixir workflow runs `mix spec.check --base origin/<base>` and then `mix spec.review` with the same base, in a separate VM. `Ancora.Review.gate_report/3` calls `Gate.check(root, review_data: true)`, so the second task redoes the full gate. On Argos with ancora 1.3.1 (4 schedulers) that is about 19 s of the review's 24 s, roughly a minute per PR in CI.

Ruling (Manuel, 2026-11-13): the no-derived-state rule in ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state was overstated. Its intent was no maintained state checked into VCS. Local uncommitted state that speeds up CI is acceptable, and the spec can be amended.

Contract:
- spec.check writes its gate core (all_findings, checked, review_data) to `_build/ancora/gate.etf`, only when git ignores that path. The write never changes spec.check's output or exit status, and a failed write is silent.
- The file carries a key: ancora module md5s and dep versions, Elixir and OTP versions, root, spec dir, base and HEAD commit ids, and a fingerprint of every dirty, untracked or (inside the scanned paths) ignored file. spec.check computes the key before and after the run and writes only if both match.
- spec.review uses the file only on an exact key match. A missing, stale, truncated or malformed file recomputes the gate as today.
- spec.check never reads the file, so the gate verdict cannot come from it.
- Amend ancora.gate.no_derived_state and the ADR, and record the ruling in a new ADR.

Proves: the review view is identical with the file absent, warm and corrupted; a warm file is really read; any key input change misses; spec.check output is byte-identical with a stale or corrupt file present; nothing is written when `_build` is not ignored. Measure Argos `spec.review` before and after.
title: spec.review reruns the whole gate that spec.check just ran
